competing_explanation: The 25% reduction could be genuine if other legitimate cost savings (e.g., lower raw-material or labor costs from the new granulation process) independently offset the misallocated solvent-recovery charge.
hypothesis_statement: VERDICT: FALSE, because the 25% cost-reduction figure is inflated by a methodological error in which the full $1.2M shared solvent-recovery line cost was charged to RX-441 under the old process and zeroed out under the new process without applying the standard allocation factor across the three products that share the line.
predicted_outcome: If the standard allocation factor were applied, the attributed cost difference would shrink substantially, yielding a materially smaller (likely far below 25%) true manufacturing cost reduction for the new formulation.
refutation_criterion: A corrected cost model applying the proper multi-product allocation of the solvent-recovery line still shows a net 25% manufacturing cost reduction for RX-441.
